CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 39-year-old female presenting with severe right upper arm pain that began approximately 18 hours ago. The injury occurred during a volleyball game when she was spiked and fell, landing directly on her right shoulder. She rates her pain as 9 out of 10. She has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours without significant relief. She has not applied ice to the injury. X-ray imaging reveals a proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies numbness or tingling in the right arm. Physical examination reveals swelling and erythema over the right shoulder with tenderness to palpation. Normal pulses noted. Remainder of examination normal. Patient able to straighten elbow without shoulder movement.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones. Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen, taken every 6 hours as needed.
Pepcid for gallstones.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert and oriented. Right shoulder with swelling and erythema. Tenderness over right shoulder. Normal pulses throughout right upper extremity. Full elbow extension and flexion maintained. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm: Proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture, right shoulder. Plan to treat conservatively with long arm cast and sling to immobilize and support the arm. Patient to follow up in 2 weeks to assess fracture healing and realignment. If fracture has not realigned adequately, surgical intervention will be considered at that time. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain. Total of 20 tablets dispensed.
